## "Midnight Sun" Zara Larsson album review

- “Euro summer isn’t over if you don’t want it to be. Zara Larsson’s fifth album, Midnight Sun, is an unbroken rush of high-energy dance-pop joy that refuses to ever slow down.” 

- Rolling Stone notes that Larsson is “celebrating the sun-drenched energy of a summer in her home country” and that the album helps keep “the good vibes, long days, and late nights going.” 

- On the title track, Rolling Stone writes: “‘Midnight Sun’ is deliriously hypnotic, with notes of trance in its swirling chorus uplifted by Larsson’s extended run.” 

- Rolling Stone groups “Blue Moon,” “Euro Summer,” and “Puss Puss” as songs that “traffic in the sweetness,” mentioning “tender scenes of short sundresses, late-night phone calls and handprints left on her ass.” 

- Describing “Girl’s Girl,” Rolling Stone notes Larsson “feels guilty for wanting a childhood friend’s man,” and in “Pretty Ugly” she sings over a stomp beat and “threatens slashed tires and crashed cars” while asking, “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this?” 

- Rolling Stone compares “The Ambition” to “the raw moments of Charli XCX’s Brat,” quoting the lyric: “But that’s the thing with the ambition / I want it so much / Everything’s a competition / So out of touch,” and calling it “one of the biggest earworm moments of the project.” 

- On “Saturn’s Return,” Rolling Stone writes that Larsson “leans into life’s confusions, giving up control she sought when she was younger,” highlighting it as a standout. 

- Rolling Stone concludes: “Those messier moments are where Larsson comes alive. You can hear her coming into her own across Midnight Sun, where even her more formulaic moments still shine brighter than that Swedish summer sun. That ambition is paying off.” 

- DIY’s excerpt via Album of the Year: “Near non-stop, Midnight Sun is entirely sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop that's both scaffolded by MNEK's production style and the Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara has readily paved.” 

- Beatroutemedia states: “Zara Larsson’s new album isn’t just a regular pop record; it’s a perfect example of how pop music should be made, and I haven’t been this hooked on an album’s sheer, great pop sound since Katy Perry’s Teenage Dream.” 

- Beatroutemedia describes the album as “a strong, cohesive record with no weak songs, where every song feels carefully crafted, from the bright, loud production to the genuine, heartfelt feelings at its core.” 

- On style, Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun is “an homage to the Scandinavian summer, giving us a vibrant, unified world of endless daylight and euphoric dance music,” and “a fun, maximalist fever dream of electro-pop that never loses sight of its heart.” 

- Beatroutemedia on "Midnight Sun" and "Blue Moon": the opening pair is called "pure fire," with the title track offering “soaring vocals over trance-inspired production” and “Blue Moon” delivering “a club-ready beat to celebrate that perfect romantic high.” 

- Regarding "Pretty Ugly," Beatroutemedia describes it as “a pure dose of chaotic energy, a rebellious, shouty cheerleader anthem that rejects the idea of being the ‘good girl’ (‘F* the ladylike, more like crazy-like’). It’s empowering, messy fun.” 

- On "Girl’s Girl," Beatroutemedia notes that it “brilliantly flips the feminist expectation of female loyalty on its head,” portraying “the horrifying, guilt-ridden feeling of crushing on a friend’s boyfriend.” 

- Beatroutemedia calls “Crush” “arguably the highlight of the entire project,” describing it as “an irresistible percussive pop jam with an amazing, show-stopping bridge” that captures “the anxiety and excitement of falling for someone totally wrong for you.” 

- For "Eurosummer," Beatroutemedia writes that it is “a total sonic shift,” a “rousing, high-energy dance beat built around hypnotic accordion melodies,” and “the ultimate party track” that “instantly transports you to a dizzying European holiday.” 

- Beatroutemedia describes “Hot & Sexy” as “a bold and confident, unavoidable declaration” that opens with “the iconic, commanding sound bite from reality TV legend Tiffany Pollard,” and suggests it cements Zara’s control over the pop scene. 

- Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun “proves that when Zara Larsson focuses her immense talent and finds her authentic sound, the result is nothing less than pure, perfect pop,” and that her growth is “a journey we can all be proud of and feel connected to.” 

- Marieltalkspop’s caption says: “I found it a little plain; all songs sound the same and only a couple kinda stand out. It’s just one more album to forget about, I couldn’t find anything interesting and I think it lacks creativity.” 

- Marieltalkspop notes that "Pretty Ugly" and "Eurosummer" were “the only two songs that stood out to me.” 

- Album of the Year lists: “Release Date: September 26, 2025” and labels “Sommer House, Epic” for Zara Larsson – Midnight Sun. 

- Album of the Year tags Midnight Sun under genres: Dance-Pop, EDM, Baltimore Club, Bubblegum Bass, Contemporary R&B, Dancefloor Drum and Bass. 

- The AllMusic snippet on Album of the Year quotes Neil Z. Yeung: “Short and sweet, this catalog highlight benefits from its length, offering just enough of what Larsson does best to have listeners craving more of this endless bliss.” 

- The DIY snippet repeated on Album of the Year reads: “Near non-stop, Midnight Sun is entirely sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop that's both scaffolded by MNEK's production style and the Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara has readily paved.” 

- Multiple professional reviewers describe Zara Larsson’s album Midnight Sun as near non-stop, sun‑drenched, high‑energy dance‑pop that functions as an homage to Scandinavian/Euro summer, combining exuberant, maximalist electro‑pop production with a cohesive emotional core. 

- The production and genre framing of Midnight Sun are widely characterized as dance‑oriented pop built on MNEK’s production style, incorporating elements tagged as Dance‑Pop, EDM, Baltimore Club, Bubblegum Bass, Contemporary R&B, and dancefloor drum and bass. 

- Beatroutemedia’s review presents Midnight Sun as a strong, cohesive pop record with no weak songs, arguing that it exemplifies how pop music should be made and praising its bright, loud production and heartfelt emotional content. 

- Rolling Stone’s review depicts Midnight Sun as an unbroken rush of high‑energy dance‑pop joy that keeps Euro‑summer vibes going and concludes that Zara Larsson’s messier emotional moments on the album are where she comes alive, with even more formulaic songs still shining and showing her ambition paying off. 

- The AllMusic excerpt (via Album of the Year) describes Midnight Sun as a short, sweet catalog highlight whose concise length showcases Zara Larsson’s strengths and leaves listeners craving more of its blissful sound. 

- A social media reviewer, marieltalkspop, criticizes Midnight Sun as plain, lacking creativity, with songs that mostly sound the same and only a couple tracks standing out. 

- Both Rolling Stone and Beatroutemedia highlight the title track "Midnight Sun" and its immediate follow‑up "Blue Moon" as a standout opening pair, describing the title song’s soaring, trance‑inflected vocals and the second track’s club‑ready beat celebrating romantic highs. 

- Critics identify several specific tracks on Midnight Sun as standouts: Beatroutemedia calls "Crush" arguably the highlight of the project, while Rolling Stone singles out "Saturn’s Return" and "The Ambition" for their lyrical focus and emotional or raw quality. 

- Reviewers from Rolling Stone and Beatroutemedia describe the tracks "Girl’s Girl" and "Pretty Ugly" as exploring messy, morally conflicted or rebellious femininity: guilt over desiring a friend’s partner and rejection of being a "good" or ladylike girl, framing these songs as empowering, chaotic expressions of complex emotions. 

- Critics note that "Euro Summer"/"Eurosummer" operates as a high‑energy party track that shifts sonically with hypnotic accordion melodies and, together with songs like "Blue Moon" and "Puss Puss," contributes to a sweet, sensual, summer‑romance atmosphere on Midnight Sun. 

- Beatroutemedia’s review portrays "Hot & Sexy" as a bold, confident declaration that opens with a Tiffany Pollard sound bite and suggests the track reinforces Zara Larsson’s sense of control over the contemporary pop scene. 

- Album of the Year lists Midnight Sun’s release date as 26 September 2025 and credits Sommer House and Epic as its labels, providing basic metadata for the album.

Zara Larsson’s fifth album, Midnight Sun, is an unbroken rush of high-energy dance-pop joy that refuses to ever slow down.
Rolling Stone notes that Zara Larsson is “celebrating the sun-drenched energy of a summer in her home country.”
Rolling Stone notes that the album Midnight Sun helps keep “the good vibes, long days, and late nights going.”
Rolling Stone writes that the title track “‘Midnight Sun’ is deliriously hypnotic, with notes of trance in its swirling chorus uplifted by Larsson’s extended run.”

Rolling Stone groups “Blue Moon,” “Euro Summer,” and “Puss Puss” as songs that “traffic in the sweetness,” mentioning “tender scenes of short sundresses, late-night phone calls and handprints left on her ass.”
Rolling Stone notes that in “Girl’s Girl,” Zara Larsson “feels guilty for wanting a childhood friend’s man.”
In “Pretty Ugly,” Zara Larsson sings over a stomp beat and “threatens slashed tires and crashed cars” while asking, “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this?”
Rolling Stone compares “The Ambition” to “the raw moments of Charli XCX’s Brat.”
The lyric from "The Ambition" is: “But that’s the thing with the ambition / I want it so much / Everything’s a competition / So out of touch.”
Rolling Stone calls "The Ambition" “one of the biggest earworm moments of the project.”
On “Saturn’s Return,” Rolling Stone writes that Zara Larsson “leans into life’s confusions, giving up control she sought when she was younger.”
Rolling Stone highlights “Saturn’s Return” as a standout track.
Rolling Stone concludes that Zara Larsson's messier moments are where she comes alive.
Rolling Stone states that Zara Larsson is coming into her own across Midnight Sun, where even her more formulaic moments still shine brighter than the Swedish summer sun.
Rolling Stone states that Zara Larsson's ambition is paying off.

DIY describes Midnight Sun as "near non-stop, entirely sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop that's both scaffolded by MNEK's production style and the Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara has readily paved.”
Beatroutemedia states that Zara Larsson’s new album is a perfect example of how pop music should be made.
Beatroutemedia states that they haven’t been this hooked on an album’s sheer, great pop sound since Katy Perry’s Teenage Dream.

Beatroutemedia describes the album Midnight Sun as “a strong, cohesive record with no weak songs, where every song feels carefully crafted, from the bright, loud production to the genuine, heartfelt feelings at its core.”
Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun is “an homage to the Scandinavian summer, giving us a vibrant, unified world of endless daylight and euphoric dance music.”
Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun is “a fun, maximalist fever dream of electro-pop that never loses sight of its heart.”
Beatroutemedia calls the opening pair of "Midnight Sun" and "Blue Moon" "pure fire."

“Blue Moon” delivers “a club-ready beat to celebrate that perfect romantic high.”

Beatroutemedia describes "Pretty Ugly" as “a pure dose of chaotic energy, a rebellious, shouty cheerleader anthem that rejects the idea of being the ‘good girl’ (‘F* the ladylike, more like crazy-like’).”
Beatroutemedia describes "Pretty Ugly" as empowering, messy fun.
Beatroutemedia notes that "Girl’s Girl" “brilliantly flips the feminist expectation of female loyalty on its head.”
"Girl’s Girl" portrays “the horrifying, guilt-ridden feeling of crushing on a friend’s boyfriend.”
Beatroutemedia calls “Crush” “arguably the highlight of the entire project.”
Beatroutemedia describes “Crush” as “an irresistible percussive pop jam with an amazing, show-stopping bridge” that captures “the anxiety and excitement of falling for someone totally wrong for you.”
Beatroutemedia writes that "Eurosummer" is “a total sonic shift,” a “rousing, high-energy dance beat built around hypnotic accordion melodies.”
Beatroutemedia writes that "Eurosummer" is “the ultimate party track” that “instantly transports you to a dizzying European holiday.”
Beatroutemedia describes “Hot & Sexy” as “a bold and confident, unavoidable declaration” that opens with “the iconic, commanding sound bite from reality TV legend Tiffany Pollard.”
Beatroutemedia suggests that "Hot & Sexy" cements Zara Larsson’s control over the pop scene.
Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun “proves that when Zara Larsson focuses her immense talent and finds her authentic sound, the result is nothing less than pure, perfect pop.”
Beatroutemedia writes that Zara Larsson's growth is “a journey we can all be proud of and feel connected to.”
